en-US.description: One app to manage AI agent skills across all your coding tools.
en-US.longDescription:
Skills Manager is a desktop app that keeps AI agent skills in one central library and installs them into coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini CLI. Skills can be installed from Git repositories, local folders, .zip or .skill archives, or the skills.sh marketplace, then grouped into presets, tagged and filtered, and tracked for upstream updates.
Global and project workspaces show what each agent actually sees, and skills sync to any supported tool via symlink or copy. Skills Manager also backs the library up to a Git remote for multi-device sync and records every install, remove, update, and sync operation in an activity log.
en-US.name: Skills Manager
en-US.releaseNotes:
Release date: 2026-11-03
Commit range: v1.43.2...v1.43.3
Release Overview
- Skills deployed to Antigravity now land in the folders Antigravity reads. A network hiccup during an update check no longer marks every skill from a repository as having an update. And a project folder that several agents share stays usable when only some of them are installed.
User-facing
- Antigravity finds deployed skills — Skills Manager deployed Antigravity skills to ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills, which current versions of Antigravity do not read. Global skills now go to ~/.gemini/config/skills, which the Antigravity app, IDE and CLI all read, and project skills go to <project>/.agents/skills. At the next sync, skills already deployed to Antigravity are deployed again in the new folder. Links in the old folder are removed, and copies there move into kept-copies/antigravity/ in the library, as with any change to an agent's folder. Thanks to @ZhuYichuan (#605), and to @zhirogo, who proposed the same paths earlier in #458 (#602, #461, #409, #217).
- A failed comparison no longer shows as an update — For skills installed from a folder inside a repository, the update check makes a second request that compares that folder with the installed version. When that request failed, for example over a dropped connection, every such skill from the repository showed "Update", and the badge, the notifications and auto-update all acted on it. These skills now show a failed check, keep their installed version, and are checked again next time. You can still update one from its card. Thanks to @HengYangDS (#583, #582).
- Shared project folders stay usable — In a project workspace, agents that read the same folder share one row; Antigravity, Cline, Warp and GitLab Duo all use .agents/skills, for example. The row counted as installed and enabled only when the first agent in it was. So skills could not be added there by a Warp user without Cline, by a custom agent sharing a built-in agent's folder, or by TRAE CN with its project folder set to .trae/skills and TRAE IDE not installed. The row is now usable while any agent that reads the folder is installed and enabled. Thanks to @GoodScholar for tracking this down in #489 (#633, #431, #632).
Developer & Governance
- skills-manager-cli skills check --json reports the skills from the second item above as error, with the comparison's message in last_check_error, where it used to report update_available. Skills installed from a repository root, and subpath skills already at the remote head, are unchanged. No new status is introduced (#583).
- project_agent_targets_for_record takes "installed" and "enabled" from every adapter whose project folder matches the row, not only from the adapter whose key the row carries. export_skill_to_project filters on the same state. The row still carries the first adapter's key. The regression test reads that key instead of naming it, because #605 changed which adapter comes first (#633, #634).
Current Verification
- ✅ Cross-platform build passed (macOS Intel / macOS ARM / Windows x64 / Linux x64 / Linux ARM64)
- ✅ TypeScript typecheck passed

zh-CN.description: 一个应用，统一管理所有 AI 编码工具的 Skills。
zh-CN.longDescription:
Skills Manager 是一个桌面应用，将 AI Agent 技能集中保存在一个中央技能库中，并可安装到 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Copilot、Gemini CLI 等编码工具。技能可以从 Git 仓库、本地文件夹、.zip 或 .skill 归档或 skills.sh 市场安装，然后分组为 Preset、添加标签和筛选，并跟踪上游更新。
全局工作区和项目工作区展示每个 Agent 实际看到的技能，技能可通过软链接或复制同步到任意支持的工具。Skills Manager 还支持将技能库备份到 Git 远程仓库以实现多设备同步，并通过活动日志记录每次安装、移除、更新和同步操作。
zh-CN.releaseNotes:
发布日期：2026-11-03
递交范围：v1.43.2...v1.43.3
发布概览
- 部署给 Antigravity 的 Skill 现在会放进它实际读取的目录。检查更新时遇到网络抖动，同一仓库的 Skill 不再全部显示有更新。项目里几个 Agent 共用的目录，只装了其中一部分 Agent 时也能正常使用。
用户可见更新
- Antigravity 能找到部署的 Skill 了 — 之前 Antigravity 的 Skill 部署到 ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills，新版 Antigravity 不读这个目录。现在全局 Skill 部署到 ~/.gemini/config/skills（Antigravity 的 App、IDE 和 CLI 都读这里），项目 Skill 部署到 <项目>/.agents/skills。已部署给 Antigravity 的 Skill 会在下次同步时重新部署到新目录。旧目录里的链接会被删除，副本移到技能库的 kept-copies/antigravity/ 下，和其他 Agent 目录变更时的处理一样。感谢 @ZhuYichuan（#605），也感谢更早在 #458 提出相同路径的 @zhirogo（#602、#461、#409、#217）。
- 比较失败不再显示为有更新 — 对于从仓库里某个子目录安装的 Skill，检查更新时会再发一次请求，比较这个子目录和已安装的版本。这次请求失败时（比如网络连接断开），同一仓库的这类 Skill 会全部显示「Update」，角标、通知和自动更新也都据此行动。现在这些 Skill 会显示检查失败，保留已安装的版本，下次检查时再试。仍然可以在卡片上手动更新。感谢 @HengYangDS（#583、#582）。
- 共用的项目目录保持可用 — 在项目工作区里，读同一个目录的 Agent 会合成一行，例如 Antigravity、Cline、Warp 和 GitLab Duo 都用 .agents/skills。之前这一行只看排在第一位的 Agent 是否已安装、已启用，所以以下几种情况都无法在这一行添加 Skill：没装 Cline 的 Warp 用户；和内置 Agent 共用目录的自定义 Agent；没装 TRAE IDE、又把 TRAE CN 的项目目录改成 .trae/skills 的用户。现在只要读这个目录的 Agent 里有一个已安装并启用，这一行就能使用。感谢 @GoodScholar 在 #489 中定位到这个问题（#633、#431、#632）。
开发者与治理更新
- 对于上面第二条里的那类 Skill，skills-manager-cli skills check --json 现在报 error，比较的报错放在 last_check_error 里，之前报的是 update_available。从仓库根目录安装的 Skill，以及已经在远端最新提交上的子目录 Skill，行为不变。没有新增状态（#583）。
- project_agent_targets_for_record 现在根据项目目录与这一行相同的所有 adapter 来判断「已安装」「已启用」，而不只看这一行的 key 所属的 adapter。export_skill_to_project 按同一状态过滤。这一行仍用第一个 adapter 的 key。回归测试改为读取这个 key、不再写死，因为 #605 改变了排在第一位的 adapter（#633、#634）。
当前校验状态
- ✅ 跨平台构建通过（macOS Intel / macOS ARM / Windows x64 / Linux x64 / Linux ARM64）
- ✅ TypeScript typecheck 通过
